definitions.type: spatial Laplace operator applied componentwise to u
definitions.definition: For x in R^n and t>0, Δ_xu(x,t)=sum_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t), component by component. The notation u_t,u_tt,∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_j}u_t denotes the corresponding classical partial derivatives on R^n×(0,∞). D_xu is the m-by-n matrix with columns ∂_{x_j}u, and |D_xu|^2 is its Frobenius square sum_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|^2. Vectors have the Euclidean dot product and norm. Spatial integrals are Lebesgue integrals on R^n; boxes carry the restricted Lebesgue measure. int denotes topological interior and 1_A denotes the indicator of a set A.
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+sum_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2, for x in R^n and t>0, with exactly the Euclidean and Frobenius normalization of problem.md:38-46.
For every t>0, E(t)=∫_{R^n} e(x,t) dx. This is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral, used after spatial integrability has been established; there is no factor 1/2.

inputs.statement: For every t0>0, put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. There exist a compact C⊂R^n and R>0 with C⊂(-R,R)^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and r∈J. Put Q=[-R,R]^n; its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. Every positive-order partial derivative of u is zero on (R^n\C)×int J. For each r∈int J the following scalar spatial functions are continuous, bounded on Q, zero outside C, and Lebesgue integrable on R^n: e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, u_t·∂_{x_j}u, ∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for each 1≤j≤n. Consequently e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable for every t>0.

argument.text: Fix t0>0. The scalar product rule and equality of mixed partial derivatives, valid because H002 is joint smoothness on the open space-time domain, give for every x∈R^n and r>0: e_t(x,r)=2u_t(x,r)·u_tt(x,r)+2sum_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u(x,r)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r). In particular e_t is continuous on that domain.

produces.statement: For all x∈R^n and r>0, e_t(x,r)=2u_t(x,r)·u_tt(x,r)+2sum_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u(x,r)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r), and e_t is continuous on R^n×(0,∞).

argument.text: Set J=[t0/2,3t0/2], choose the compatible C and R>0 furnished by N002, and set Q=[-R,R]^n. For every r∈int J, e(·,r), e_t(·,r) and the terms in F001 are continuous and integrable, and vanish outside C⊂int Q. In particular E(t0) and the nearby energy integrals are finite by N002 and D003.

produces.statement: For r∈int J, e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t(·,r)·u_tt(·,r) and ∂_{x_j}u(·,r)·∂_{x_j}u_t(·,r) for 1≤j≤n are integrable and zero outside Q. Q is compact and |Q|=(2R)^n<∞.

argument.text: Choose eta=t0/4. Then [t0-eta,t0+eta]=[3t0/4,5t0/4]⊂int J. The continuous function |e_t| from F001 is bounded on the compact set Q×[t0-eta,t0+eta]; the extreme value theorem supplies a finite nonnegative bound. Thus there exists B≥0 such that |e_t(x,r)|≤B for every x∈Q and r∈[t0-eta,t0+eta].

produces.statement: There exists B∈R with B≥0 and |e_t(x,r)|≤B for every x∈Q and r∈[t0-eta,t0+eta]; this time interval is contained in int J.

argument.text: Choose such B from F003. Define the total function v(h,x)=(e(x,t0+h)-e(x,t0))/h when 0<|h|<eta, and v(h,x)=0 otherwise. The density is evaluated only at positive times in the first branch. Define bnd(x)=B 1_Q(x). Q is a measurable box of finite measure by F002; hence bnd is integrable and its absolute integral is B|Q|<∞. For every 0<|h|<eta, H002 makes the two densities in v continuous in x; their scalar difference quotient is continuous and therefore strongly measurable as a real-valued function.

produces.statement: bnd is Lebesgue integrable on R^n. For every h with 0<|h|<eta, the spatial function v(h,·) is continuous and hence strongly measurable, since it is a scalar multiple of a difference of continuous real-valued densities.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary h∈R and x∈R^n. Temporarily assume L1: 0<|h|<eta. For x∈Q, apply M004 to the one-variable function r↦e(x,r) on the interval with endpoints min(t0,t0+h), max(t0,t0+h), and derivative r↦e_t(x,r). For purposes of the source's global domain R, extend both by zero at nonpositive times; the entire closed interval lies in (0,∞), where H002 and F001 give continuity and the asserted derivatives. The endpoints are distinct by L1. The source gives the difference quotient as e_t at an intervening time (the quotient is the same for either sign of h). By F003 its absolute value is at most B. For x∉Q, both densities vanish by F002, so the quotient is zero. The cases together prove |v(h,x)|≤B1_Q(x)=bnd(x). Discharge L1 and quantify over x and h to obtain: for all 0<|h|<eta and all x∈R^n, |v(h,x)|≤bnd(x).

produces.statement: For every real hh with 0<|hh|<eta and every xx∈R^n, |v(hh,xx)|≤bnd(xx).

argument.text: Let ell be the punctured-neighborhood filter at 0 in R. It is countably generated: the punctured intervals 0<|h|<1/k for positive integers k form a countable base. F004 gives strong measurability of v(h,·) for all sufficiently small nonzero h, and integrability of bnd. F005 gives domination everywhere in x for those h. For each x∈R^n, differentiability in time from H002 and F001 gives v(h,x)→e_t(x,t0) along ell. Instantiate M001 with X=R^n and Lebesgue measure, V=R, I=R, this ell, F(h)=v(h,·), f(x)=e_t(x,t0), and bound bnd. All these conditions hold pointwise or eventually as required, so ∫v(h,x)dx→∫e_t(x,t0)dx as h→0, h≠0.

For 0<|h|<eta, F002 ensures that both densities in v are integrable. By linearity of the Lebesgue integral and D003, ∫v(h,x)dx=(E(t0+h)-E(t0))/h. Thus F006 proves differentiability of the actual finite function E at t0, with E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0)dx. Substitute F001 and use the integrability of all its terms from F002 and linearity over the finite spatial sum: E'(t0)=2∫u_t·u_tt dx+2sum_{j=1}^n∫∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t dx. All integrands are evaluated at t0. The choices were available for arbitrary t0>0, so universal introduction proves every clause of the exported conclusion.

applications.bindings: For each current x∈Q and 0<|h|<eta, take f(r)=e(x,r), d(r)=e_t(x,r), extended by zero for r≤0; set a=min(t0,t0+h), b=max(t0,t0+h).
hypothesis_checks: H002 and F001 make e(x,·) continuous on the closed interval, which F003 places in int J⊂(0,∞).
H002 and the product-rule identity F001 give the classical derivative e_t(x,r) throughout the open interval; extension at nonpositive times cannot affect this local derivative.

applications.bindings: Set X=R^n, mu=Lebesgue measure, V=R, I=R, ell=punctured neighborhoods of 0, F(h)(x)=v(h,x), f(x)=e_t(x,t0), and source bound=bnd.
hypothesis_checks: Euclidean R^n has its Borel/Lebesgue measurable structure and Lebesgue measure; R is a real normed vector space. The punctured intervals 0<|h|<1/k give the required countable filter base, as displayed in S006.
F004 proves strong measurability for 0<|h|<eta, which is an ell-eventual condition since eta>0.
F005 proves domination for every x for 0<|h|<eta; in particular it holds almost everywhere and ell-eventually.
F004 establishes integrability of bnd=B1_Q because Q is measurable of finite measure and B≥0 is finite.

For each fixed x, H002 and F001 identify the pointwise difference-quotient limit as e_t(x,t0); v is that quotient for ell-eventually all h. This pointwise conclusion implies the required almost everywhere convergence.
